A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpatialReward research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching figures moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-benchmark evaluations, OmniGen2 RL experiments, ablations, attention analyses, and latency measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds RL evaluation using UniRef-Image-Edit in Section 5.3 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The Think-with-Boxes mechanism, separate SC/PQ streams, data pipeline, reward aggregation, and SFT/GRPO training procedure remain unchanged. The UniRef experiment applies the existing pipeline; region-level rewards are proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: Training-data sources and evaluation coverage remain unchanged, including EditReward-Bench, MMRB2, MER-Bench, GEdit-Bench, and ImageEdit-Bench. The added UniRef experiment uses existing benchmarks and does not establish a new task or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds the unaligned UniRef-Edit baseline as the control for its SpatialReward-aligned counterpart. The reward-model comparator sets in Tables 1–2 and all previous OmniGen2 comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds UniRef-Image-Edit as a stronger policy-backbone configuration for the existing RL evaluation. The existing benchmarks, metrics, and previously stated training protocols remain unchanged; detailed UniRef-specific settings are not supplied.

E4.justification: The added stronger-editor experiment explicitly tests whether SpatialReward's downstream benefit depends on OmniGen2. Existing spatial-grounding and aggregation ablations, attention diagnostics, grid search, training-dynamics analyses, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains the same attention statistics with ± reporting and N = 776. The new UniRef results are point estimates, with no added run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds UniRef results: GEdit-EN overall increases from 7.46 to 7.56 and ImageEdit-Bench from 4.15 to 4.23 after alignment. GEdit SC changes from 7.81 to 8.02, while PQ decreases from 7.83 to 7.81. Previously reported benchmark, OmniGen2, ablation, attention, and latency results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The structured-output definition, reward aggregation, SFT and GRPO objectives, and attention-metric definitions in Appendix C.1 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and substantive conclusion retain the same claims about attention collapse, spatial grounding, SpatialReward-260K, MER-Bench, and effective online RL. The additional backbone experiment supports the existing applicability claim without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly interprets the UniRef experiment as evidence that improvements extend beyond OmniGen2. The conclusion adds a substantive future direction: region-specific rewards and per-edit advantage estimation could provide denser credit assignment than the current single-scalar reward.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Tables 6–7 identify NVIDIA H800 GPUs where v1 specified only GPUs, retaining the same device counts and hyperparameters. The front-page access link changes from a GitHub repository to a dedicated project website. These are documentation changes, not evidence of changed hardware or newly available resources.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to stylized handwritten-text generation, Joint Reward Modeling, and UniRef-Image-Edit. Related work briefly acknowledges concurrent auxiliary language supervision, while the paper's central positioning around explicit spatial grounding remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized related-work expansions, a new stronger-editor paragraph, a condensed conclusion with future work, and added acknowledgements and a generic impact statement. Author/conference footnotes and cross-references are updated, while the main section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn as a full-width horizontal pipeline. v1 appendix Figures 7–8 move into the main text as v4 Figures 5–4, Table 3 gains a UniRef block, and appendix figures are resized or repositioned. Most visual content, axes, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly strengthens validation by testing a second, stronger editor and improves reproducibility through explicit H800 disclosure. The enlarged pipeline figure and more prominent benchmark documentation also aid reading. The gains are limited: the core evidence is unchanged, and the added experiment lacks uncertainty estimates and competing reward-model comparisons, with a small PQ decline despite higher overall scores.
